newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends rangebound session weaker.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends rangebound session weaker.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended moderately lower and toward the bottom of the day's slim range Tuesday, pressured by a late-session round of local selling, market sources said.

Dealers said locals were searching for sell-stops beneath yesterday's low of 104.50 cents a lb in the active March contract, but steady scale-down trade buying and roaster interest near that level stemmed losses.
March coffee slumped to a low of 104.90 cents before settling at 105.10, down 0.95 cent on the day. March reached a high of 106.75. Spot December futures finished down 0.50 cent, to 114.30.
On the charts, traders said March's next support level was seen at 101.50, with strong psychological support at the 100.00-cent mark. Resistance was pegged at 107.50 cents.

Traders said the market was largely technically driven, with market participants brushing aside the latest CSCE certified stock data. The CSCE reported after the close of business Monday that U.S. certified coffee stocks were unchanged at 321 60-kg bags in the week ended Nov. 29, the lowest level since the CSCE began tracking stocks in 1980. The CSCE said 2,500 bags of coffee were pending grading in Miami.
In other news, the Mexican Coffee Council said Tuesday Mexico exported 163,489 60-kg bags of coffee in October compared to the 131,912 bags sold abroad in the same month a year ago.
